_about: The poses a toy takes on a story's frames (references/frames.md): each a set of joint turns (radians, XYZ; the joints toy.json names: body, head, armR, armL, legR, legL) and the view it is usually seen from. `run.mjs poses` renders them from the film's own toy on a clear background (build/poses/); film.json "poses" adds a film's own in the same shape. A toy with no arms or legs plays them with its body and head. The same joints move the toy in the film (engine/lib/beatkit.js: startle, duck, slump, push, kick, lookUp, shrug, holdUp).

holdUp.says: both arms up: holding a sign, a prize, a thing over its head

startle.says: thrown back, arms flung up: a surprise, good or bad

duck.says: head down, arms over it: something is coming down

slump.says: head hanging: at a loss, tired, let down

shrug.says: arms out, head to one side: well, then

lookUp.says: head back, looking up at something big

push.says: leaning into a weight with both arms (from its side, so the weight stands before it: `push:left` for one on the left)

kick.says: one leg out: kicking something away (from its side, to the left of the frame: `kick:right` kicks to the right)

point.says: its right arm out at something (seen from its left, it points to the left of the frame)

pointLeft.says: its left arm out (seen from its right, it points to the right of the frame)

present.says: one arm raised to what stands behind it: here it is

speak.says: one hand up before its mouth: a microphone, a word to the viewer

balance.says: arms out, feet apart: riding something

cheer.says: arms straight up (behind a big head they hardly show: holdUp reads better from the front)
